get.description: Answers the calls the api key consumed in the current throttling window, day and month, the calls it is allowed to make, and the calls it has left. The admin behind the credentials has to be able to read the api and the api key. The api key has to be authorized on the api, directly (`api_<apiId>` in its `authorizedEntities`, or minted by one of the plans of the api) or through one of the groups of the api.

get.summary: List the api keys of an api
get.description: Answers the api keys authorized on the entity with this id, directly or through one of its groups, that the admin behind the credentials can read. With at least one of the `clientId`, `name`, `group` and `enabled` filters, only the api keys matching one of them (they are not combined) are answered, and the `page` and `pageSize` parameters paginate them; without filter every api key is answered. The entity is looked up among the legacy service descriptors, the routes, the route compositions and the apis: the api keys of an api are the ones authorized on it (`api_<apiId>`, or minted by one of its plans) or on one of its groups. An audit event is sent.

parameters.name: apiId
parameters.description: The id of the entity whose api keys are listed. Meant to be the `id` of an api, it is looked up among the routes, the route compositions and the legacy service descriptors (see the description)

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: Keeps the api key with this client id

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Keeps the api keys with this `clientName`

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Keeps the api keys authorized on the group with this id

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Keeps the api keys enabled (`true`) or disabled (`false`)

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to answer, starting at 1, when a filter is given. 1 when absent

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The number of api keys of a page, when a filter is given. Every api key is answered when absent

200.description: The api keys authorized on the entity that the admin behind the credentials can read, as an array of api key entities (a page of the matching ones when a filter is given)

schema.description: The api keys authorized on the entity

400.description: The credentials are missing (the route that serves the admin api refuses the call before the controller runs), `page` or `pageSize` is not a number, or `enabled` is not a boolean

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

404.description: No service descriptor, route, route composition or api has this id

An api that exposes no route answers zeros. An id that is not the one of an api, but of another entity the admin can read (a route, a route composition, a draft), answers an empty object. The admin behind the credentials has to be able to read the api: an id that is not the one of an api, a route, a route composition or a draft is not found. An audit event is sent.

post.summary: Subscribe to a plan of an api
post.description: Saves the subscription of the body, in the `pending` state, as a draft subscription with `version=Draft`. The api of the path has to be enabled, neither deprecated nor removed, and the plan of the path published. The subscription is then checked against its own `api_ref` and `plan_ref`: the api has to be in the `staging` or `published` state, the plan in the `staging` or `published` state, and the `subscription_kind` has to be the access mode of the plan. For an `apikey` or an `oauth2-local` plan, an api key is minted from the plan and referenced in the `token_refs` of the subscription. The admin behind the credentials has to be able to write the api. An audit event is sent.
